name: The bridge's light when it loses the switches

artboards.title: Today · Every drop shows at once; red after about 24 seconds
A · A minute's grace: a drop under a minute never shows
B · Red is only for placing; the wall says the rest
C · A shaky link is one calm color, not three

annotations.text:
WHY THIS IS BEING DRAWN

23 November, while setting up the stairway: "The puck LED is showing different status colors rapidly. Is this really a sign of unstable connection or is it a bug?"

What the hub could see: no restarts, no broker drops, no update running. But the bridge reported "far" (breathing red), its link had moved between three different switches during the day at -71 to -75 dBm, and once it lost the switches entirely until it was replugged. It sits nearest the main bedroom switch, then under cabinet, then the stairway; all three are on the house's own network.

So the light was telling the truth about a link that kept dropping. The question for these boards is whether it should tell it like that. Why the link drops is a separate question, for the bridge's own log.

TODAY -- FROM THE CODE

One rule picks the color every pass (puck/src/lightrule.h): not well -> blinking amber, or breathing red once the mesh module has had three empty scans in a row (about 24 seconds); placed and well -> the nightlight, or dark.

Red was made for placing (design/puck/Placing.dc.html): somebody is standing at a socket asking "is here good?", and red means "no, try nearer a switch". Once the bridge is placed, nobody is asking. A restarted switch or a shaky minute then reads as an alarm, and a link that comes and goes reads as a strobe: warm, amber, red, warm.

What stays whichever is picked: faults outrank the nightlight (light.h). A light that glows warm while the bridge can't reach anything is furniture that lies, so every direction still shows a loss that lasts. They differ in how soon, and in which color.

A -- A MINUTE'S GRACE

For a placed bridge only. The light keeps showing what it showed for the first minute after a drop; amber after a minute, red after three.

Calmest of the three: the restart and the shaky link never show. That is also its cost. A link that drops for 50 seconds every minute is a broken bridge, and the light shows nothing at all. It lies for a minute at a time, which is the thing light.h says the light must not do.

B -- RED IS ONLY FOR PLACING

Once placed, the bridge never goes red: a drop shows as blinking amber at once, for as long as it lasts. After five minutes the wall says it on the Needs a look line, "The bridge can't reach the switches", because a household reads the wall, not a socket.

Honest second by second, and it gives a long loss to the screen that can explain it. But the shaky link is still a strobe, warm and amber over and over, which is the thing that was asked about.

C -- ONE CALM COLOR FOR A SHAKY LINK

A drop under 20 seconds doesn't show: that is a switch restarting or a moment of noise. Anything longer turns the light a slow amber, a breath, not a blink. It stays slow amber until the link has held for a whole minute, so a link that comes and goes reads as one steady "shaky" rather than three colors. Red only after five minutes with no switch at all, when moving the bridge really is the answer.

The restart case costs a minute of slow amber: the light owns up to the drop, calmly, and clears once the link has proved itself.

RECOMMENDED: C

It answers the question that was asked. A shaky link becomes one calm color, so the light stops looking like a fault in the light. It stays honest: a loss that lasts still shows, which A gives up. And red keeps its one meaning, move me, which B spends on a timer nobody sees.

B's wall line is worth taking with it: after five minutes, the Needs a look line on the wall says the bridge can't reach the switches, so the household hears it on the screen they read.

Built, it is the rule in lightrule.h with a memory of how long the link has been down and how long it has held, and a fourth look (the slow amber) in light.cpp. The mesh module's three empty scans stop deciding red on their own.
